decisions.question: q-38079

source.question: q-38079
source.value:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ uv\end{aligned}].
$$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-38079

source.question: q-38079
value: :answer.type/text
The critical points lie on the lines $v=\pm u.$
source.rationale: For T(u,v)=(u²+v²,uv), the derivative matrix has rows (2u,2v) and (v,u), so its determinant is 2(u²−v²). It vanishes exactly on v=u or v=−u, original option c. The authentic solution's derivative list has a typo stating ∂(uv)/∂v=v; its subsequent matrix correctly uses u and reaches the correct determinant and conclusion. Saved grading reports Correct. The stored key denotes the identical pair of lines.

decisions.reason: Persistent repair judgment from authentic worked solution and original choices supersedes stored key

decisions.question: q-81319

source.question: q-81319
source.value:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+3y \\ 2x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$
